narrative_summary: Geopolitical friction and economic strain dominate current affairs as the expanding war with Iran disrupts global shipping lanes, drives up domestic borrowing costs, and fuels inflation that continues to batter the administration's public approval ratings. Domestically, federal policy shifts are sparking intense scrutiny and legal battles, ranging from controversial prison transfers and proposed rewrites of scientific research funding toward artificial intelligence to trade restrictions targeting Chinese technology. Concurrently, technological investments face productivity skepticism as the AI sector matures, while political strategists monitor shifting electoral dynamics and legislative house race ratings ahead of upcoming primaries. Across multiple fronts, institutional resilience is tested by economic headwinds, foreign entanglements, and ongoing debates over public trust and institutional oversight.

source_summaries.title: Right-Wing Media and OnlyFans Are in a Symbiotic Relationship
bullets: Internet personality Savanna Cannon combines standard MAGA political talking points with provocative physical poses in her short-form videos.
Cannon uses her political content strategy to attract a male audience and drive traffic to her OnlyFans subscription page.
This phenomenon reflects a broader symbiotic relationship between right-wing media influencers seeking larger audiences and OnlyFans creators looking for new subscribers.

source_summaries.title: Civil Disobedience Is Coming to Springfield
bullets: Economic growth slowed to 1.5 percent in the second quarter as the expanding Iran war strains the national economy and disrupts global shipping lanes.
The imminent expiration of temporary protected status for over ten thousand Haitian immigrants in Springfield, Ohio, is resulting in job losses and community distress.
Local religious leaders and coalitions are urging federal authorities to halt widespread deportations and are bearing the financial burden of assisting affected residents.

source_summaries.title: Todd Blanche’s New Grip on the Federal Prison System
bullets: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche faced scrutiny during his confirmation hearing over the minimum-security prison transfer of Ghislaine Maxwell following his interview with her.
Lawmakers and former prison officials argued that Maxwell's placement violated standard Bureau of Prisons regulations and appeared to be a politically motivated reward.
Critics warn that a broader policy shift centralizing prison placement authority under the attorney general could enable the administration to reward allies or punish perceived enemies.

source_summaries.title: How Trump made America less popular than China
bullets: Recent Pew polling shows that China is now viewed more favorably than the United States in Canada, Mexico, and most major European countries.
Donald Trump's second-term foreign policy has severely damaged America's international reputation through pointless threats of invasion and diplomatic conflicts with close allies.
The negative global shift in public opinion is driven by the economic fallout from the war with Iran and Trump's antagonistic rhetoric toward friendly nations.

source_summaries.title: The case against homeownership
bullets: Homeownership contradicts standard financial advice to diversify assets by tying a massive share of savings into a single property.
While buying a home offers stability, rent insurance, and acts as a savings commitment device, policies heavily tilt in favor of homeowners.
The broader debate centers on whether cultural narratives and the policy landscape should shift away from encouraging homeownership.

source_summaries.title: Microsoft Soars, Meta Sinks: Has The AI Narrative Flipped?
bullets: Ed Elson and Gil Luria analyze the contrasting earnings reports of Microsoft and Meta to evaluate the direction of the AI sector.
Mike Gapen discusses the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and why rates may remain stagnant throughout the year.
Ed Elson shares his perspective on FIFA's decision regarding the sale of its profits.

source_summaries.title: A Heavy Wave.
bullets: US borrowing costs reached their highest level since 2007 as the Federal Reserve held rates steady amid fears of an inflationary shock from the conflict with Iran.
American forces launched a heavy wave of strikes against dozens of targets in Iran following ballistic missile attacks on US forces in Jordan.
Reports indicate that the Houthis, advised by Iran's Revolutionary Guards, are considering implementing a toll system for the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

source_summaries.title: Andy Beshear Set Out to Make Drug Treatment Widely Available in Kentucky. Fraud and Abuse Followed.
bullets: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear lifted Medicaid restrictions in 2020 to expand access to drug treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic.
The relaxed oversight led to soaring state spending, reaching $2.3 billion for behavioral health and addiction treatment by 2024.

Health industry experts and the state attorney general warned of widespread Medicaid fraud and subpar care by unscrupulous providers, though Beshear defended the policy by pointing to declining overdose deaths.

source_summaries.title: Completing the picture of the court’s criminal law term
bullets: The Supreme Court decided 41 criminal law and related cases this term, making up about 60% of its total merits opinions.
The court's official website divides judicial writings into "Opinions of the Court" and "Opinions Relating to Orders," though both must be examined to fully understand the justices' legal views.
Of the 16 pure criminal law cases decided on the merits after full briefing, 11 were decided in favor of the criminal defendant's view.

source_summaries.title: How a seemingly unexciting case on retirement plans could have massive consequences
bullets: The Supreme Court will decide in Anderson v. Intel Corporation Investment Policy Committee whether ERISA lawsuits over underperforming retirement investments must identify a meaningful benchmark at the pleading stage.
The case involves Intel's retirement plan fiduciaries who shifted investment strategies toward limiting volatility and losses rather than maximizing returns during a historic bull market.
Federal circuits are split on whether plaintiffs must provide a sound basis for comparison when alleging fiduciary imprudence based on comparative underperformance.

source_summaries.title: Justice Kavanaugh: the great concurrer of the Roberts court?
bullets: Justice Brett Kavanaugh frequently writes concurring opinions that distinguish his approach from that of past judicial archetypes like the playmaker or the great dissenter.
Kavanaugh's concurrences generally serve to demonstrate respect for losing parties, educate the public on the court's reasoning, or outline his views for future cases.
In recent terms, Kavanaugh has consistently remained in the court's majority while frequently utilizing separate opinions to stake out middle paths and signal potential future legal developments.

source_summaries.title: Trump indicates that he will bring Hillary Clinton case to SCOTUS
bullets: President Donald Trump has indicated he will ask the Supreme Court to revive his failed lawsuit against Hillary Clinton and the Democratic National Committee.
Trump requested an additional month to seek review of an appeals court decision that upheld the dismissal of the case and affirmed nearly $1 million in sanctions.
The 11th Circuit Court of Appeals previously ruled that Trump and his lawyer filed a frivolous lawsuit and waited too long to sue.

source_summaries.title: LAI #136: Build Faster With Agents, Debug Their Failures, and Evaluate Them More Reliably
bullets: AI engineering is shifting focus toward building reliable production systems and improving agent evaluation methods.
A practical evaluation trick involves running LLM judge comparisons twice in reverse order to detect and mitigate position bias.
Community projects like Hoshi provide agents with isolated cloud environments to execute tasks directly using code and shells.

source_summaries.title: We Drafted The Perfect Primary Calendar
bullets: The current presidential primary system developed largely through historical accident rather than deliberate design.
Democrats are reshuffling the early-state calendar for the 2028 election by dropping Iowa and placing South Carolina and Nevada ahead of New Hampshire.
A newly proposed Democratic National Committee calendar outlines six states to vote before Super Tuesday.

source_summaries.title: Live with Phillips P. OBrien and Ivanna Ryzhkova
bullets: This post provides a recording of a live video discussion featuring Phillips P. OBrien and Ivanna Ryzhkova.
The content includes a guest post contributed by Ivanna Ryzhkova.

source_summaries.title: China Deepens Military Support for Iran
bullets: China is reportedly preparing to supply Iran with 300 to 400 advanced shoulder-fired surface-to-air missile systems.
The transfer aims to help Tehran rapidly rebuild its air defenses following months of conflict with the United States and Israel.
This move marks a shift from Beijing's historical preference for quiet support to actively helping Iran recover military capabilities during an active regional war.

source_summaries.source: Free the Inquiry by Heterodox Academy
source_summaries.title: Liberal faculty are surprisingly bullish on political diversity
bullets: A national survey by Heterodox Academy found that a majority of faculty believe all eight examined dimensions of diversity improve teaching and research.
Liberal faculty were surprisingly more likely than others to report that political diversity enhances teaching and research across most disciplines.
Faculty collectively underestimate how much their peers value political and religious diversity, which contributes to academic self-silencing.

source_summaries.title: 🔮 For AI adopters, success and failure look identical — at first
bullets: Companies are investing heavily in artificial intelligence, yet broad adoption has not yet visibly lifted overall economic productivity.
Technology investments like AI follow a J-curve where expensive upfront learning and process changes occur long before financial returns materialize.
Successful and failing AI rollouts can look identical at first because high initial costs and mistakes make both appear expensive and unproductive.

source_summaries.title: Sabato's Crystal Ball - Thirteen House Rating Changes - Vol. 24, Iss. 53
bullets: Sabato's Crystal Ball updated 13 House race ratings to better align seat-by-seat assessments with overall expectations for November.
Democrats remain favored to flip the House majority, though Republicans retain a path to victory.
The number of House Toss-up races increased from 15 to 20 as part of the latest update.

source_summaries.title: Five Things to Know About the DSA
bullets: The Democratic Socialists of America wield influence in the Democratic Party that exceeds their formal membership numbers.
Prominent figures associated with or supported by the American far left include Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Zohran Mamdani, and Hasan Piker.
DSA founder Michael Harrington historically favored pragmatic support for major party nominees to challenge incumbent Republicans, contrasting with some contemporary socialists.

source_summaries.title: Sabato's Crystal Ball - Georgia Senate: The Peach State Ripens for Democrats - Vol. 24, Iss. 52
bullets: Sen. Jon Ossoff is becoming a stronger favorite to win a second term as Democratic prospects in Georgia improve.
Ossoff has maintained a formidable financial advantage, raising over $20 million in the second quarter of 2026 and holding $42 million on hand.
Sabato's Crystal Ball shifted its rating for the Georgia Senate race from Leans Democratic to Likely Democratic.

source_summaries.title: AI & Robotics enters Escalating U.S. Protectionism Phase
bullets: The Trump administration unveiled bans targeting imports of new Chinese robots and power inverters to protect the U.S. AI buildout and reshore key industries.
The Federal Communications Commission and the U.S. Department of Commerce are implementing strict measures and export controls to counter foreign technology competition.
The administration is also deliberating whether to extend these bans to include Chinese open-weight models.

source_summaries.source: Don Moynihan from Can We Still Govern?
source_summaries.title: Watching the show trials
bullets: The article argues that the primary institutional failure during the pandemic was political rather than related to public health.
Unlike other countries, the United States uniquely descended into political psychosis and conspiracy theories surrounding the crisis.
Republican politicians continue to target public health officials for blame and retribution while avoiding their own responsibility.

source_summaries.title: The End of the American Empire? Why the Iran War Is Slipping Beyond Washington’s Control
bullets: The ongoing conflict with Iran is increasingly slipping beyond Washington's control as regional actors shape events independently.
Inexpensive missiles and mass-produced drones are challenging traditional U.S. military assumptions regarding power projection and quick victory.
Despite overwhelming military superiority, the United States struggles to secure vital maritime corridors and political objectives.

source_summaries.title: Reality is a Communist Plot
bullets: Paul Krugman argues that the MAGA movement rejects objective reality and facts in favor of beliefs that suit their prejudices.
The author cites numerous examples of false claims made by Donald Trump and his supporters regarding science, economics, and events.
Krugman compares this extreme rejection of truth to George Orwell's observations about the totalitarian mindset.

source_summaries.title: The "new science golden age" looks suspiciously like a grift
bullets: A new White House report authored by Michael Kratsios outlines a vision to reorient federal scientific research toward corporate profit and artificial intelligence.
The proposed policy marks a sharp departure from the traditional post-WWII model of funding independent, university-based basic research.
The administration has already begun shifting billions of dollars in research funds toward AI projects while cutting funding for other scientific areas.

source_summaries.title: Why a Strait of Hormuz Consortium Will Likely Fail
bullets: Tehran rejected a recent Omani proposal for a regional consortium to manage Strait of Hormuz traffic because it lacked sufficient authority over shipping lanes.
A maritime consortium would fail to resolve the region's underlying security dilemma and would instead institutionalize Iranian geopolitical leverage.
Unlike the peaceful evolution of the Strait of Malacca management framework, the Persian Gulf lacks the necessary history of economic and security integration.

source_summaries.title: Trump's huge hidden upward redistribution
bullets: Trump's tariffs and war with Iran are driving up prices for goods and services for American consumers.
Big American corporations and domestic producers are quietly supporting these policies because they enable price hikes and soaring profits.
The resulting economic dynamic creates a massive hidden redistribution of wealth from consumers to corporate shareholders and executives.

source_summaries.source: Heather Cox Richardson from Letters from an American
source_summaries.title: July 29, 2026
bullets: A CNN poll conducted by SSRS found that 70% of adult Americans disapprove of President Donald J. Trump's handling of the economy, with 75% disapproving of his handling of inflation and 79% disapproving regarding gas prices.
Trump's overall approval rating dropped to 34%, matching his lowest ever recorded rating from January 2021, while 50% of respondents strongly disapprove of him.
Majorities of those polled also expressed disapproval of Trump's handling of the situation in Iran, his attention to the country's main problems, and his stamina for office.
